feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning and a consistent career progression in digital communications. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but it would be more impactful with tighter consolidation, more outcome-focused metrics, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear narrative of advancement within one organization, which strengthens credibility and shows increasing responsibility.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds substance and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Summary, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; several sections restate the same capabilities and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes for email, social, web redesign, video, and governance work where possible.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” should drop the comma for consistency; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to public-sector/advocacy digital leadership would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your niche: public-sector, advocacy, and mission-driven digital communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, more senior framing around cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and operational leadership.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and integrated content strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful, but avoid repeating similar positioning elsewhere in the header/subtitle.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-value strategic capabilities over broad or repeated phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS modernization.”
- Reduce overlap by focusing on strategic strengths rather than tools or broad functions already covered elsewhere.
- Standardize phrasing so all items are parallel noun phrases and use “communications” consistently.

Suggested rewrite:
Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS modernization • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Content operations & systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats Soft Skills and header language.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider using one section or making this version more strategic and condensed.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Rephrase for outcomes and ownership: “Designed and launched…” / “Led…” / “Implemented…” instead of “Consult,” “Build,” “Deliver,” “Advise.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search relevance improvements, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… best practices” repeat themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsites, AI search, and campaign storytelling also appear in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and let the project section hold specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/ownership scope, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable business impact where possible: email growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, cost savings from in-house studio, reporting efficiency, or governance improvements.
- Tighten phrasing by removing generic verbs like “directed”/“strengthened” unless paired with results; combine tools into one concise analytics bullet rather than listing every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as scaling via the new in-house studio.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and undersells impact. Emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements while avoiding overlap with the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to stress operational leadership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector membership audience.”
- Tighten bullets and front-load outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer systems language: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; use “established/scaled” here instead of “produced” alone.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used in the 2022–2024 director entry unless you add a concrete result.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths and reduce generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and aligned with the work history.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker than the others; “audience-centered content strategy” feels more strategic.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; vary wording if keeping this section.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, with the most relevant items first: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here (for example jQuery) unless the target role explicitly requires it.
- Consider replacing “WordPress / SharePoint / Power Pages” with “Multi-platform CMS experience (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to save space and reduce listiness.
- If possible, align wording to proven impact from recent roles: “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ pages” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows” elsewhere in experience bullets, not here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led wording: “Analytics strategy, reporting infrastructure & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets for each tool.
- Replace generic phrases with outcome-oriented language tied to recent work: “KPI framework design,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “behavior and performance analysis,” “measurement for web modernization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework design and executive dashboards - SEO, user behavior and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider keeping Topline Skills capability-focused and leaving the full tool stack to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and event delivery rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more distinctive phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to sound less entry-level.
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows: “supporting advocacy programming and recurring executive/event content.”
- Keep to 3–4 items max; this section should scan quickly and complement, not repeat, the detailed experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; use more specific wording here.
- PTZ camera systems and studio operations also overlap with “Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT, so avoid repeating tool-level language elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just nouns: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing via GitHub Pages**
- If Drupal is your clear differentiator, foreground it more strongly: **Drupal-led CMS modernization • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation details for the coding/technical section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or differentiating this one with proficiency/context.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so avoid repeating that phrase unless this item is rewritten to add specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for delivery/integration: “Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in parentheses: “GitHub Actions (deployment automation)” or “Google Tag Manager (tracking implementation)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML, CSS” is cleaner and more current

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both sections
- If space is tight, keep newer/distinctive tools here (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, GTM) and leave core coding languages in Topline Skills only

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as an undifferentiated tool dump. It also overlaps with stronger, more strategic language elsewhere, so it should emphasize systems you actively used to build workflows rather than generic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Tighten to higher-signal tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration tools (**Slack, Teams**) out unless they were used for workflow automation/admin, not just communication.
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a pure list: **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project and editorial operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with **Topline Skills: “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems.”** Keep this section tool-specific and let the Topline Skills section carry the strategic framing.
- **Basecamp** and **Trello** may dilute the section unless they were materially used in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory. Make it more specific to email/engagement operations and align it with the stronger email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten phrasing to emphasize function: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add capability keywords instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey orchestration**
- Best stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email campaign operations, audience segmentation, newsletter publishing, engagement workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is partially supported by recent work-experience bullets on newsletters and digital channel leadership; avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this entry tool-focused, not strategy-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split the rest into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and recurring weekly video updates, and expanded in-house digital content capacity.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or efficiency gains from new workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; specify what was built or improved.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory at NACo. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs, especially the podcast launch, while avoiding overlap with later digital-team roles.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Supported innovation and policy research initiatives across NACo programs, translating findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast achievement the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific deliverables if possible: web articles, interviews, audio segments, briefing materials, or multimedia packages.
- If you can quantify anything, add it: number of episodes launched, stakeholders/program teams supported, or recurring series established.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid emphasizing broad digital operations or team-building here; those are covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production” repeats across multiple entries, so this item should focus on research-to-content translation and the first podcast launch.
